intro: Samoa, the 'cradle of Polynesia', keeps one of the strongest traditional cultures in the Pacific.

chapters.title: Polynesian heartland
text: Lapita people arrived about 3,000 years ago, and Samoa became a starting point for voyages across Polynesia. Chiefs called matai led extended families.

chapters.title: German and New Zealand rule
text: In 1899 Germany took the western islands (today's Samoa) and the US the eastern ones (American Samoa). New Zealand took over in 1914. The 1918 flu killed about a fifth of the people, and New Zealand police killed peaceful Mau protesters in 1929.

highlight.title: The Mau
highlight.text: A peaceful independence movement whose motto was 'Samoa for Samoans'.

chapters.title: Independence
text: In 1962 Samoa became the first Pacific island nation to win independence in the 20th century. In 2011 it skipped a day, moving west of the International Date Line. Fiamē Naomi Mataʻafa became the first woman prime minister in 2021.

timeline.title: Divided
timeline.text: Germany and the US split the islands.

keyTerms.meaning: A chief who leads an extended family.
